notes: The marginal alternative *ward against ward, as well etc.* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).

`לְעֻמַּת` → *all alike* fuses under rule 30 read as one rendering rather than one token: neither morpheme owns *all* or *alike*, and the unit heads on the construct noun (rule 23) and on *alike* (rule 31).

The Hebrew writes a comparative particle for each member, so rule 14's correlative pair does not arise; *as well* is the first particle's own rendering, and marking *well* `added` was the competing reading.
`מִשְׁמֶרֶת` carries no suffix, so the supplied *their* is `added` under rule 18's closing sentence while the supplied *for* belongs to the bare nominal under rule 33.
